To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

goldfish possess three SRIF genes, and that the three SRIF mRNAs have different brain distributions and show differential seasonal variations, but that only one of the three SRF mRNAs is closely related with the seasonal variations in serum GH levels and brain SRIF-14 contents.

goldfish brain expressed three SRIF mRNAs, encoding SRIF-14 (with sequence identical to mammal), [Glu1,Tyr7,Gly10]SRIF -14, and [Pro(2)]SRIF-14; the mRNAs were differentially distributed in the brain, with differential seasonal variations in the levels, and [Pro]SRIF- 14 was biologically active.

the goldfish brain contains three distinct PSSs, that the levels of the mRN As encoding PSS-I and PSS-II are differentially and seasonally regulated, and that the putative SRIF variant, [Pro 2]SRIF14 is biologically active in goldfish.
In summary, our research is concerned with
three distinct SRIF genes in goldfish brain.

the characterization and distribution of three PSSs and the seasonal variation in the levels of their mRNAs and the identification and characterization of the biologically active form, [Pro2 ]SRIF-14.
the molecular cloning, brain distribution and seasonal variations of the mRN As encoding PSS-I, -II and -III and the biological activity of the putative SRIF peptide, [Pro2]-SRIF-14.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the three SRIFs are differentially distributed in the brain and that the levels of the mRN encoding PSS-I and PSS-II are differentially modulated by the season, with the seasonal variation of the PSS-I mRNA being associated with that of serum GH levels.

goldfish brain produces three distinct preprohormones, PSS-I, -II, and -III, and the three PSSs are translated and cleaved to yield three distinct SRIF peptides, SRIF-14 (with sequence identical to mammal SRIF-14), SRIF-28 and [Pro2, Tyr7, Glu10]SRIF, respectively.
the goldfish brain contains three SRIFs, which are differentially distributed and seasonally altered in levels, with differential actions on GH release from the goldfish pituitaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

three distinct SRIFs, SRIF-14 (PSS-II), [Pro2]PSS-III, and [Glu1,Tyr7,Gly10]PSS- III, were identified in goldfish brain and pituitary, and the three SRIFs may play distinct roles in the brain-pituitary axis.

goldfish possess three distinct prepro-SRIFs, with the preproSRIF-I and -II encoding the putative precursor proteins of SRIF-14 identical to mammalian and teleostean SRIF-14 (SRIF-I and SRIF-III), and the preproSRF-III encoding the precursor protein of the novel putative SRIF variant, [Pro(2)] SRIF-14.

the goldfish brain has three distinct PSS genes and the expression of the PSS genes in goldfish brain is regulated differentially in a tissue-specific and seasonal manner, with PSS-I being involved in the control mechanism of the seasonal variation of serum GH levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

three distinct PSSs, encoding three distinct SRIFs, are expressed in the goldfish brain, and that the three PSSs and their encoded SRIFs are differentially distributed, differentially regulated in a sex-dependent manner, and have distinct roles in seasonal control of GH secretion.

the three distinct SRIF mRNAs were differentially expressed in goldfish brain and the seasonal variation in the level of the mRNA encoding the putative biologically active SRIF-14 was closely correlated with the seasonal changes in brain SRIF-14 content and serum GH levels.

the three PSSs are differentially regulated in goldfish brain, with the mRNA encoding PPS-I being the most abundant and the one that is most closely related to the seasonal variation in GH release and serum GH levels.
